title: Reconstructing an internal action by free restriction and right translations
statement:
Work in compatible universes and small skeletons [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $J$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, let $P$ be the profinite site with finite jointly surjective covers [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $P_J$ have profinite continuous left $J$-spaces, continuous equivariant maps and finite jointly surjective covers [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $H(S)=J\times S$ with left translation on $J$, and $tS=S$ with trivial action [def-sfb-profinite-action-parameters]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(P)$ and let $\mathscr E^{\underline J}$ be the category of internal actions: a sheaf $X$ with a natural unital associative action $C(S,J)\times X(S)\to X(S)$ [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. Write $h_T(S)=C(S,T)$, with the induced action when $T\in P_J$. For every $F\in\operatorname{Sh}(P_J)$, the presheaf
$$G(F)(S)=F(H(S)),\qquad G(F)(f)=F(\operatorname{id}_J\times f)$$
is a sheaf on $P$. For $g:S\to J$ define the continuous equivariant map $r_g:H(S)\to H(S)$ by $r_g(j,s)=(jg(s),s)$. The operations
$$g\cdot x=F(r_g)x\qquad(g\in C(S,J),\ x\in G(F)(S))$$
give an internal left $\underline J$-action on $G(F)$. In particular, $F(r_1)=1$, $F(r_g)F(r_h)=F(r_{gh})$, and for $f:V\to S$ one has $G(F)(f)(g\cdot x)=(g\circ f)\cdot G(F)(f)(x)$. Every sheaf map $F\to F'$ induces an equivariant map $G(F)\to G(F')$ by its components on $H(S)$, defining a functor $G:\operatorname{Sh}(P_J)\to\mathscr E^{\underline J}$. Moreover
$$H(S_i)\times_{H(S)}H(S_j)\simeq H(S_i\times_SS_j)$$
by $((j,s_i),(j,s_j))\mapsto(j,s_i,s_j)$, naturally in the maps to $S$, and $H$ carries finite jointly surjective covers to such covers.

proof.text: The site and the acting group sheaf. By [lem-sfb-profinite-action-finite-cover-site], the indicated finite families define the site $P_J$, and continuous maps to any profinite target satisfy descent on $P$. Apply its latter assertion with target $J$: $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$ is a sheaf. Pointwise multiplication, unit and inverse preserve continuity because $J$ is a topological group and commute with precomposition; the group identities hold pointwise. Thus this is the group sheaf used below. The same assertion supplies the representable sheaves $h_T$ on $P$ appearing in the statement, with pointwise induced action when $T$ has a $J$-action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), auxiliary free-restriction construction; argument written by Q105

proof.text: Free parameters preserve covering pullbacks. Use the actual functor $H$ of [def-sfb-profinite-action-parameters]. For maps $a:A\to S$, $b:B\to S$, a point of $H(A)\times_{H(S)}H(B)$ is a pair $((j,a_0),(k,b_0))$ with $j=k$ and $a(a_0)=b(b_0)$. The stated map to $H(A\times_SB)$ therefore has inverse $(j,a_0,b_0)\mapsto((j,a_0),(j,b_0))$. Both maps are continuous by their coordinate formulas, equivariant for left translation, and inverse. The projections commute with these maps, so the identification is natural. If $\{S_i\to S\}$ is finite jointly surjective, then each $(j,s)$ lifts to $(j,s_i)$ for some lift $s_i$ of $s$; hence $\{H(S_i)\to H(S)\}$ is finite jointly surjective. If the family is empty, its target is empty and so is $H(S)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), auxiliary free-restriction construction; argument written by Q105

proof.text: Restriction is a sheaf. Step 2 verifies both conditions for continuity of $H:P\to P_J$: it preserves every covering family and the fibre products along its covering arrows (indeed all the indicated pullbacks). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf] with $u=H$ and $\mathcal G=F$. Its conclusion gives the sheaf $G(F)=F\circ H$, with exactly the displayed restrictions. Concretely, a compatible family in $F(H(S_i))$ is compatible on $F(H(S_i\times_SS_j))$, hence, by step 2, on $F(H(S_i)\times_{H(S)}H(S_j))$; the sheaf condition for $F$ glues it uniquely to $F(H(S))$. The empty cover gives a singleton since $H(\varnothing)=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tags 00WV (definition-continuous), 00WW (lemma-pushforward-sheaf), applied to the explicit pullback and cover formulas of step 2

proof.text: Right translations give a left action. For a continuous $g:S\to J$, multiplication in $J$ makes $r_g(j,s)=(jg(s),s)$ continuous; it is equivariant since $(aj)g(s)=a(jg(s))$. Thus $F(r_g)$ is defined. Pointwise calculation gives $r_1=\mathrm{id}$ and $r_h\circ r_g=r_{gh}$, since $(jg(s))h(s)=j(g(s)h(s))$. Contravariance gives $F(r_1)=\mathrm{id}$ and $F(r_g)\circ F(r_h)=F(r_h\circ r_g)=F(r_{gh})$. For $f:V\to S$, the identity $r_g\circ H(f)=H(f)\circ r_{g\circ f}$ follows by evaluating both sides at $(j,v)$, where both equal $(jg(f(v)),f(v))$. Applying $F$ gives $G(F)(f)F(r_g)=F(r_{g\circ f})G(F)(f)$. The operations therefore define a natural map $\underline J\times G(F)\to G(F)$ satisfying the unit and associativity equations, which is exactly an internal action by the definition in [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction].

source.place: Paragraph (3), auxiliary free-restriction construction; argument written by Q105

proof.text: Functoriality in the sheaf. For a sheaf map $\alpha:F\to F'$, put $G(\alpha)_S=\alpha_{H(S)}$. Naturality of $\alpha$ for $H(f)$ gives the sheaf-map restriction equation, and naturality for $r_g$ gives $\alpha_{H(S)}F(r_g)=F'(r_g)\alpha_{H(S)}$. These are precisely equivariant morphisms of the action category defined in [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. Since components of identity and composite natural transformations are identities and composites, $G(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $G(\beta\alpha)=G(\beta)G(\alpha)$. This defines the asserted functor with all the prescribed formulas.
